rationale: PINS the operator-application and constructor-application shapes VERIFY_HS9 added on 2026-10-04, and the negatives that keep them honest. Every shape was confirmed against the PINNED GRAMMAR with script/m14/tmp/hs9-ast-dump.ts BEFORE this file was written, and the file parses with hasError=false (248 nodes): `a :+: b` is match -> infix with field operator = constructor_operator; `a `Snoc` xs` is match -> infix -> infix_id -> constructor; `(<+>) x 1` is match -> apply -> prefix_id -> operator; `(.+.) :: Int -> Int -> Int` is signature -> name: prefix_id -> operator. PINS: (1) a locally declared operator's application sites are calls, across four syntactic positions (plain RHS, GUARD, case branch, and a forward-referenced prefix application); the two guard sites are a COUNT PIN, because they share source|target and differ only by line, so a dedupe-key regression collapses them silently. (2) an infix CONSTRUCTOR's application is instantiates and never calls. (3) a TICKED constructor's application is instantiates. (4) a prefix operator application is calls. NEGATIVES, each the failure the rule could plausibly make: an operator DEFINITION head emits nothing; a PATTERN-position infix constructor (`uncons (n :+: rest)`) emits nothing; a TYPE-position operator whose spelling is also a value operator in the same file emits nothing (`type Shifted = Int .+. Int`); a Prelude operator this file does not declare emits nothing (`++`, `intercalate`, `replicate`); and a raw head text never becomes a symbol name. NOT PINNED, and deliberately so: `:+:` and `Snoc` are constructor names carried on the grammar's INFIX data-constructor shape (grammar/data.js `_datacon_infix`), which extractConstructorName cannot name, so no Constructor symbol and no `contains Chain -> :+:` edge exist for them. That is measured in the lane report against the full corpus, not asserted here.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: the two guard sites (69 and 70) share source|type|target and differ only by line. A per-set dedupe-key regression collapses them to 1 and this pin fails; a drop of both fails the two line pins above as well.

TWO construction sites on one line (`a :+: (b :+: c)`), same source|type|target and same line, so the lane's `source|type|target|line` dedupe key yields exactly ONE edge. Pinned so the collapse is a recorded decision rather than an accident: this is the dimension-8 key, and the neighbouring multi-site group above is distinguished by line.

forbidRelationships.comment: NEGATIVE (c) `uncons (n :+: rest) = ...` MATCHES an infix constructor; matching constructs nothing. The grammar puts this in a `patterns` node, and the rule gates on that.
NEGATIVE (c), the other label: a matched constructor is not a call either

NEGATIVE (b) `type Shifted = Int .+. Int` is a TYPE expression. `infix` is one node type for three positions in this grammar (_exp_infix / _pat_infix / _type_infix are all aliased to `infix`, with the same field names), so a type-level operator is a bare `operator` node exactly like an expression's. If the position test were missing this edge would appear.
NEGATIVE (a) `++` is Prelude's and this file does not declare it. Name resolution: only an operator the file declares is a target.
NEGATIVE (a) an imported name is not a target (the FP-family rule)
NEGATIVE (a) an imported Prelude name is not a target
the definition body `a * 10 + b` uses Prelude operators; neither is declared here, so the operator publishes no callers beyond its real ones
the guard condition `x > y` uses Prelude's `>`, which this file does not declare
the definition body `a + b` uses Prelude's `+`

NEGATIVE (c, ticked shape) `lengthOf (_ `Snoc` rest) = ...` MATCHES a ticked constructor in a function head pattern. Matching constructs nothing. This is the HSD14 rule applied to the shape VERIFY_HS9 added: without the gate, every pattern match of a ticked or infix constructor would be published as a construction.

NEGATIVE (d) an operator DEFINITION head is not a call. `a .+. b = a * 10 + b` names `.+.`; the head is not an application of it, and the body calls only `*` and `+` (both Prelude). Without the pattern-position gate this edge would appear — the HSD19 rule applied to operator heads.
NEGATIVE (d) the same for a PREFIX_ID operator head: `a <+> b = a + b` names `<+>` and does not apply it.

expectComplexity.comment: measured, not guessed: `| x > y = ... / | otherwise = ...` is a `guards` node and each guard set is a decision point in this lane's complexity model, so the symbol's complexity is 1 base + the guard sets. Written after the first run reported 3 against my assumed 1.
